stem: During neck dissection, a nerve loop is injured. Sternohyoid, sternothyroid and omohyoid become weak, while thyrohyoid and tongue movement remain intact. Which structure was injured?

options.label: A
options.explanation: Injury to its motor fibres would weaken the tongue; the stem specifically preserves tongue movement.

options.label: B
options.explanation: It supplies the diaphragm, rather than this group of infrahyoid muscles.

options.label: C
options.explanation: This C1–C3 loop supplies sternohyoid, sternothyroid and omohyoid, matching the selective deficit.

options.label: D
options.explanation: It supplies sternocleidomastoid and trapezius, rather than these strap muscles.

options.label: E
options.explanation: It supplies most intrinsic laryngeal muscles rather than the three infrahyoid muscles listed.

context: Ansa cervicalis supplies three infrahyoid muscles. Thyrohyoid receives C1 fibres travelling with the hypoglossal nerve, so it can remain intact after injury to the loop.
